New instrument scripts/checks/fleiss_kappa.py, **verified against an answer it did not compute**: it reproduces Fleiss' published worked example (10 subjects x 14 raters x 5 categories) at kappa=0.2099 vs the published 0.210. 12 locks, and the important ones are refusals -- a RAGGED table (a reader silently skips an arc) is rejected rather than averaged, because the quantity it would return is not Fleiss' kappa but would be reported as one; a single-category margin is rejected rather than returned as 1.0, which would read as "the panel agrees perfectly" when the panel never discriminated anything; an out-of-vocabulary label stops the gate rather than being binned. **B815's pre-data note was committed while the workflow was still running and no rating had been seen**: on synthetic data of wave 2's exact shape (12x15x4) at 85% per-rater fidelity, kappa=0.7695 with bootstrap CI [0.6549, 0.8471]. So the 0.75 gate is a DEMANDING bar (~85%+ per-rater fidelity across a 4-category vocabulary), and **15 items cannot resolve it to better than about +/-0.10** -- the CI straddles the threshold. **The sealed gate is NOT loosened** (kappa>=0.75 to write, below to hold, exactly as sealed; moving a threshold after building the instrument that measures it is the same error as moving a falsifier). What is added is a REPORTING obligation, strictly more honest and never more permissive: a pass whose CI lower bound falls below the gate reports as PASS (marginal), a fail whose CI upper bound sits above it as HOLD (marginal), interval printed either way. The caveat's whole credibility is its timestamp -- recorded now it constrains the reading whichever way the data lands. Measurement of the INSTRUMENT, not the object; Gate 5 untouched.

## B816 — the reproducible audit sampler, committed before its verdicts exist (2026-07-30)
Wave 1 audited the first three arcs of each reader's slice and got 36/36 -- an uninformative number for a STRUCTURAL reason, not a statistical one: the first arcs of a slice are the ones a reader judged while freshest, and anyone choosing WHICH arcs to audit after seeing the verdicts can land on an agreeable set without meaning to. A 100% pass rate on a set selected that way is compatible with a substantial error rate on the rest. scripts/checks/audit_sample.py replaces it with a rule fixed in advance: sort the frame lexically, seed with the committed constant 20260730, sample without replacement -- the draw is a function of (frame, seed) and nothing else. 7 locks on the property that matters, which is not randomness but UN-STEERABILITY: reproducible; independent of input order (reordering the frame cannot change the sample); without replacement; it tracks the FRAME not the auditor (adding one arc changes the draw -- the honest direction of dependence); a different seed gives a different draw, so quietly re-seeding for a friendlier set is a VISIBLE act rather than a silent one; and the seed constant is locked as part of the preregistration rather than left a knob. Committed before the wave-2 verdicts it will audit exist -- as with B815 the ordering is what makes it honest, the code is nearly trivial. Repository-instrument scope; Gate 5 untouched.

## B817 — Wave 2: reader-bias confound RESOLVED; the gate was narrower than the work (2026-07-30)
12 readers x (15 shared calibration + 47 disjoint) = 564 work judgements + 180 calibration judgements. **Fleiss' kappa = 0.9312** (12 raters, 15 shared items), CI [0.7485, 1.0000]; sealed gate kappa>=0.75 -> PASS, verdicts WRITTEN, flagged **PASS (marginal)** per B815's pre-committed rule because the CI lower bound sits 0.0015 below the gate -- pedantic, and applied anyway, because a rule honoured only when comfortable is not a rule. **THE RESULT WAVE 1 COULD NOT REACH:** on the IDENTICAL block, 10 of 12 readers produced the exact same verdict mix (5 NEGATIVE / 10 PROVED), the other two 7:8 and 6:9 -- the conservatism offset is essentially nil, so wave 1's 0.364->0.917 per-slice PROVED-rate spread was NOT reader bias: **the eras genuinely differ.** Only 2 of 15 arcs drew any disagreement (B429 10:2, B755 11:1); 13 unanimous. **THE FLAW THIS RUN FOUND IN ITSELF:** the calibration block exercised only TWO of the four verdict categories (all 12 readers used only PROVED/NEGATIVE) while the work used four -- so kappa certifies agreement on a two-category distinction and was used to license a four-category one, saying nothing about OPEN, which is exactly where wave 1's disagreements lived; 13.1% of work judgements and 3.7% of written verdicts fall in untested categories. The calibration arcs were selected without checking they exercised the vocabulary they were meant to calibrate -- the vacuity lesson one level up (the criterion could not even be EXERCISED across the range it governed). Locked by a test so it cannot quietly become untrue. **Writer safety held under a live 3.0% fault rate:** all 17 readers hitting a nonexistent arc returned OPEN + "no frontier directory exists", ZERO fabrications; 216 authored verdicts not overwritten; 31 no-FINDINGS skipped; B58 (3 candidate dirs) skipped rather than guessed. **299 written; coverage 317 -> 616 of 746 (42.5% -> 82.6%).** **Audit 20/20**, drawn by B816's committed seed over the frame of what actually landed, AFTER the writes so it could not be steered -- unlike wave 1's uninformative 36/36 on first-three-of-each-slice; includes B780 written RETRACTED (matching its post-B784 header not its original claim), B616 written OPEN rather than rounded up, and B786's claim stopping at its own content instead of reaching into B787's later 4th-involution refinement. Carried: a calibration block exercising all four categories checked BEFORE the run, and the 11 OPEN/RETRACTED writes re-read under it; 130 arcs still unverdicted, mostly dirs with no FINDINGS.md. Gate 5 untouched.

## B818 — the 2 errors wave 2's untested vocabulary let through (2026-07-30)
B817 recorded that its own calibration block exercised only TWO of four verdict categories while licensing four-category work, leaving 11 writes in untested territory -- recorded as a limitation because it was not then known whether any were actually wrong. **They were checked. Two are wrong, and both fail at exactly the untested boundary.** All 8 RETRACTED verdicts were read against their arcs' own text: six correctly withdraw THEIR OWN headline (B192 "REFUTED", B216 "OVERTURNED", B90 "CORRECTED", B437, B731, B780); two do not. **B745** ("the B742 revivals (B58,B225) cross-verified -- CONFIRMED x2", established by re-execution PLUS five independent checks of its own with a working negative control -- the cat map fails the identity as it must) and **B525** (the 61-agent adversarial re-audit: 4 CONFIRMED / 2 SHAKY / 3 CRACKED, master negative PHYS-REFUTED surviving all five lenses) both WITHDRAW OTHER ARCS' RESULTS WHILE ESTABLISHING THEIR OWN -> corrected to PROVED. Labelling an auditor RETRACTED makes the ledger say the audit is untrustworthy, the exact opposite of what these arcs established. **Methodological catch:** a screening regex flagged five as suspect because it searched only for RETRACT/WITHDRAWN -- three were FALSE POSITIVES (B192 says REFUTED, B216 OVERTURNED, B90 CORRECTED); reading them rather than trusting the screen is what kept three CORRECT labels from being "fixed" into wrongness ("a first count is a hypothesis", earning its keep again). **New PRACTICES rule:** RETRACTED applies only when the arc withdraws ITS OWN headline; an arc establishing that ANOTHER arc's claim fails is labelled by what IT established, and the retraction lands on the TARGET's record -- which is what makes the label usable, since RETRACTED on X means "do not trust X's old claim" and that is the only thing it is good for. Locked by a test checking every RETRACTED arc carries a self-retraction marker (wide vocabulary, to avoid the same false-positive trap). **Carried, honestly not closed:** the retractions these auditors trigger are NOT recorded on their targets -- B519_re_mining carries NO verdict though B525 cracked its "no external crossing" headline; B225 carries PROVED though B745 confirmed its 2-half kill vacuous (may be correct for B225's surviving content -- needs reading, not assuming); B58 is split across 3 directories and was skipped for that reason. Fixing needs judgement about what still stands, not bookkeeping. **Scale of the original flaw, measured rather than feared: 2 errors in 11 untested-category writes (18%); 0 in the 20-arc random audit of the tested categories** -- real, bounded, exactly where B817 predicted. Gate 5 untouched.

## B819 — CORRECTION to B817: the verdict residue is a coverage-FRAME gap, not a data gap (2026-07-30)
B817 stated the remaining unverdicted arcs were "mostly directories without a FINDINGS.md". **That is wrong**, and it matters because it tells a reader there is nothing to do. In fact **133 of the 181 unverdicted directories (73%) DO have a FINDINGS.md**; of those, 17 were assigned to a wave-2 reader and skipped as duplicate-directory arcs (B58 -> 3 dirs), and **116 were never assigned to any reader at all**. Repository-wide: 791 distinct arc ids in frontier/, 579 assigned to some reader, **229 never assigned**. So 116 arcs carry real findings that no reader was ever given -- they were not judged and found wanting, they were never in the frame. **How the error happened:** I read the residue's shape off the run's failure counters (31 no_FINDINGS_md, 17 no_directory), which describe ONLY the arcs that were assigned; generalising them to the whole residue is a sampling error, because the assigned set is exactly the set that is not representative of what was left out. The campaign's "coverage -> ~99%" expectation was unreachable from the start, since the frame was 73% of the repository and nothing in the run measured frame against repository. **The anticipated "non-standard layout" category has exactly ONE member:** B519_re_mining (CAMPAIGN.md + VERDICT.md, no FINDINGS.md), correctly refused by writer safety -- and it is the arc most in need of a RETRACTED marker, since B525 cracked its "no external crossing" headline; 45 further dirs hold only README/PREREGISTRATION/campaign files. **Next:** a third wave over the 229 unassigned ids closes ~116, with a calibration block exercising all four categories (B817 section 3, now in PRACTICES). NOT to be read as 116 more PROVEDs -- they are unjudged, and since the wave-1 era spread is now known to be REAL rather than reader bias, an unsampled era's rate is not predictable from the sampled ones. **Transferable: a coverage number is only as good as its frame, and the frame must be measured against the REPOSITORY, not against the work list.** Same shape as B817's own calibration flaw -- a measurement correct about what it measured, used to speak about something larger. B817 corrected in place; test_b819_frame_gap locks the correction. Gate 5 untouched.

## B820 — the lexicon gate fired; the RATE says it is rotting, not merely outgrown (2026-07-30)
The fail-closed atlas-lexicon-current gate BLOCKED a push at 21 zero-motif probes against a ceiling of 20 -- doing exactly what it was built for. **The count alone could not justify a response**, and that is a design limit worth naming: an absolute count on a growing corpus fires eventually no matter how good the lexicon is, so raising the mark on that basis would be indistinguishable from silencing the gate. **So the rate was measured, and it settles it:** arcs from B770 on are blind at **12.2%** against **2.3%** for everything earlier -- **5.4x**. New work is five times more likely to be invisible to the atlas than old work: the lexicon is ROTTING, not merely outgrown. **The gate now reports both count and rate**, so a future firing carries its own diagnostic and states which of the two it is -- that is the durable fix; the ceiling was never the interesting number. The mark is raised 20 -> 21 as an explicit DEBT MARKER with the reason written into the code beside it ("this raise buys one step, it does not absolve"). **The lexicon refresh is now DUE and is the next instrument task**; it moves every atlas figure and needs its own seal, which is why it was not folded into a correction commit. Overall blindness is 21/746 = 2.8%, and the blind set includes B798, which defines the programme's own current falsifier -- the exact case the gate's docstring named when it was written. Repository-instrument scope; Gate 5 untouched.

## B821 — the lexicon refresh FAILED its sealed criteria; the failure CORRECTS B820 (2026-07-30)
Prereg 590aeb5021478197 sealed at 52f8169e before any LEXICON edit (it moves every atlas figure). **VERDICT: FAILURE, reverted per the seal.** The new instrument-layer motif matched 5 of 7 substantial blind arcs (criterion 1 passed) but **46.2% of the corpus against a 25% ceiling** (criterion 2 failed). The vacuity ceiling fired exactly as written -- a motif catching the 7 by matching half the repository would make the atlas LOOK healthier while telling a reader less. **My pre-stated expectation was SUCCESS; it was wrong**, and the seal is what makes that a result rather than an embarrassment. **Why it failed:** the self-audit vocabulary is not a topic in this corpus, it is the AMBIENT REGISTER of the house method -- "prereg" appears in 27.6% of arcs, "audit" 14.7%, "census" 11.6%. A motif must DISTINGUISH, and "the programme examining itself" cannot, because nearly a third of all arcs preregister. **A wiring bug was caught by the sealed criteria on the FIRST run:** the anchor "bridge_construction" exists in TWO dicts (LEXICON and OBSTACLES) and the edit landed in OBSTACLES, whose values are keyword LISTS; the obstacle classifier would have iterated the dict's KEYS and silently scored every arc against kind/gloss/patterns. 0/7 matched and 0.0% of corpus -- an impossible result for a live motif -- flagged it instantly. An argument for two-outcome criteria on INSTRUMENT changes, not only on claims. **THE BLIND COUNT DECOMPOSES, AND THIS CORRECTS B820:** B820 read the 12.2% vs 2.3% rate as "the lexicon is rotting"; that reading is WRONG. The 21 blind arcs are 14 THIN STUBS (409-1988 bytes against a 4078-byte median -- nothing to match), 6 PURE-INSTRUMENT arcs (correctly invisible, since the atlas is an OBJECT lexicon and these have no object content), and **1 genuine gap: B537**, the Markov-type surface x2+y2+z2-xyz=c and SL(2,Z) trace triples. **The real lexicon gap is ONE arc, not twenty-one**; the 5.4x rate reflects a shift in what the programme has been DOING, not decay. B820's instrument improvement stands (the rate diagnostic is what made this decomposition easy to ask for); its diagnosis is corrected. **Consequently: do not refresh the lexicon on the strength of the blind count.** The one addition worth making is a character-variety/Markov-surface motif for B537 -- NOT done here, because this arc's seal was spent on a different hypothesis and reusing it would be moving the goalposts. The gate metric should exclude stubs and instrument arcs; that needs its own seal. **Transferable: a gap in a measuring instrument is not the same as a defect, and the difference is COMPOSITION** -- "21 arcs are invisible" and "the lexicon is failing" looked like the same statement for two commits, and were not. Gate 5 untouched.

## B822 — the lexicon gate stops diagnosing; its ratchet turns out self-referential (2026-07-30)
Prereg 69a7ae603dc5a1dd sealed at 884e825f before the edit. **SUCCESS on both sealed criteria:** the size floor removed 14 of 22 blind arcs (needed >=10), leaving 8 (needed <=10); pre-stated expectation was "14 removed, leaving 8" -- exactly that, recorded as a confirmation, which is weaker evidence than a surprise. **What triggered it:** immediately after B821 banked, the gate fired printing "the lexicon is ROTTING, not merely outgrown" -- the exact inference B821 had just refuted -- and the arc that pushed it over was B821 ITSELF, a pure-instrument arc an OBJECT lexicon is correct to miss. A gate was emitting as a machine verdict a claim the repository had disproved one commit earlier. **Two changes:** the metric is floored at FINDINGS.md >= 2000 bytes (a 409-1988 byte arc reading "Logged observation, not a claim." cannot match any lexicon; counting it measured the ARCHIVE's shape, not the instrument's health), and the ROTTING-vs-outgrown verdict text is REMOVED -- the gate now reports count, ceiling, thin-arcs-excluded and the list, and asks the reader to decide "whether each is a real gap or an arc an OBJECT lexicon should miss". It reports; it no longer concludes. **Deliberately NOT done: hand-excluding instrument arcs** -- that classifies by TOPIC, a judgement about arcs this seat wrote, and would let the number be tuned by relabelling; size is objective, topic is not, so six of the remaining eight are instrument arcs and stay counted. **THE STRUCTURAL LIMIT THIS RUN EXPOSED: writing B822's own findings file broke the ceiling it had just set (8->9)**, because the arc documenting the gate is itself a substantial instrument arc. The gate ratchets against instrument arcs and every future one will increment it -- bumping each time is the pattern this arc was written to stop. Ceiling set to 9 including this file, mechanism stated rather than papered over; the threshold is the wrong SHAPE and no value of it is right. B823 replaces it with a triage registry (each substantial blind arc explicitly recorded as a real gap or as correctly-missed, gate failing only on UNTRIAGED ones), which removes the number entirely. **The three-commit sequence, worth stating because the shape recurs:** B820 "the lexicon is rotting" (diagnosis wrong, rate diagnostic useful) -> B821 one motif closes it (failed its own vacuity ceiling at 46.2%, reverted, decomposed the count into 14 stubs + 6 instrument + 1 real gap = B537) -> B822 the gate should stop diagnosing. The instrument was wrong in a way that LOOKED like a finding for two commits, and what caught it was not scepticism but COMPOSITION -- asking what the 21 arcs actually were. Gate 5 untouched.

## B823 — the lexicon gate becomes a TRIAGE REGISTRY: no threshold, a judgement per arc (2026-07-30)
B822's ceiling was self-referential: writing the arc that documented the gate incremented the count the gate was measuring, and every future instrument arc would do the same -- bumping it each time is the exact pattern B821/B822 were written to stop. **There is now NO CEILING.** Every substantial blind arc (FINDINGS.md >= 2000 bytes) must carry a disposition in docs/atlas/BLIND_ARCS.md -- GAP (a real object topic the lexicon misses; open instrument work) or INSTRUMENT (an arc about the programme's own machinery, which an OBJECT atlas is CORRECT to miss and which must NOT be closed by adding a motif, since B821 proved a meta-layer motif matches 46% of the corpus) -- and the gate fails ONLY on UNTRIAGED arcs. State: 9 substantial blind arcs, all triaged; **1 open GAP: B537** (Markov-type surface x2+y2+z2-xyz=c, SL(2,Z) trace triples); 14 thin arcs excluded. **The same self-reference recurs and now resolves CORRECTLY:** B823's own arc went blind and demanded a row -- under B822 that forced a meaningless act (bump a number), under B823 a meaningful one (state whether it is a real gap and record it where a reader can check). The self-reference did not go away; it stopped being a problem, because the response it demands is now informative. **The gate can actually fail -- verified, not asserted:** three negative controls (remove a row -> "NOT triaged"; add a row for a non-blind arc -> "no longer substantial-and-blind"; delete the registry -> "the triage registry is this gate's only input"), each required to fail by a lock. The stale-row check matters as much as the missing-row check -- a gate that only checks for ABSENCE would let the registry rot. **Honest failure mode, stated rather than hidden:** labelling everything INSTRUMENT; that is VISIBLE (a reviewer reads the rows and the reasons) in a way a quietly-raised ceiling never was -- making the failure mode legible was the goal, eliminating it is impossible while a human classifies. B822's locks were re-anchored on the properties that survive rather than the wording B823 superseded (a lock pinned to a superseded literal tests the past, not the invariant). **Four commits, from a number to a judgement:** B820 "rotting" (diagnosis wrong) -> B821 one motif (failed its own vacuity ceiling at 46.2%, decomposed the count) -> B822 stop diagnosing (succeeded, then broke its own ceiling by being written) -> B823 stop counting. **A measuring instrument that reports a number nobody can interpret will eventually be tuned rather than read.** Gate 5 untouched.

## B824 FAILED / B825 SUCCEEDED — the last known lexicon gap closes (2026-07-30)
**B824 (prereg 3ba7eacea2d19002, attempt 1): FAILURE at 18.4% against a 15% ceiling, reverted.** My declared worry was WRONG -- I predicted criterion 3 (redundancy with trace_map) would be the danger, since trace_map carries Fricke.Vogt and the Markov surface IS the Fricke level set; it was not redundant at all (76.8%, and against firewall). The kill came from the ceiling I expected to clear. **The diagnosis is B821's lesson one level down:** "character variety" alone carries 13.8% of the corpus -- this programme's SUBJECT MATTER, not a topic within it, structurally identical to "prereg" at 27.6% making B821's meta-motif ambient. B821's failure was about the ambient METHOD; B824's about the ambient OBJECT. **B825 (prereg 2812a0c550ae2b92, attempt 2 of a cap of 2): SUCCESS on all three criteria, IDENTICAL and not relaxed** -- hits B537; 8.3% of corpus (<=15%); 75.8% max containment (<90%). Only the patterns changed, and the change APPLIED B824's own measurement (drop the one ambient term; keep the Markov cubic and trace triples, every remaining pattern having measured <=4.1%) rather than searching for a passing configuration. **Pre-stated expectation was SUCCESS "near 6-9%"; it landed at 8.3%** -- recording the predicted RANGE is what makes that a real check, since a pass at 14.5% would have cleared the ceiling while revealing far more pattern overlap than assumed. **The attempt cap did its job by existing:** two attempts declared BEFORE attempt 2 ran, because "iterate the patterns until the share clears the ceiling" has no stopping rule and would eventually yield a passing motif by SEARCH rather than insight; the cap was not reached, but it is what makes the success interpretable. **docs/atlas/BLIND_ARCS.md now shows 0 open GAP rows**, which the registry states in place means "no known uncovered object topic among substantial blind arcs" and NOT "the lexicon is complete" -- B806's call for a full re-grounding is untouched. **A known false-positive mode is recorded rather than filtered:** B821/B822/B823 left the registry not because they are ABOUT the Markov cubic but because they QUOTE it while discussing the gap -- a regex motif matches MENTIONS, not SUBJECTS; filtering it would mean classifying by topic, which B822 refused because it lets the number be tuned by relabelling. **Six arcs, and the instrument that ends the sequence is not the motif -- it is the ceiling that refused the first two.** Three superseded locks were re-anchored on enduring invariants rather than deleted (a lock pinned to state that legitimately changed tests the past, not the invariant). Gate 5 untouched.

## B826 — B519's missing verdict was a FILENAME gap, not a content gap (2026-07-30)
B519_re_mining carried no verdict at all though B525 had cracked its "no external crossing" headline; B818 called it "the arc most in need of a RETRACTED marker" and B819 found it the ONLY arc in the repository with a non-standard layout (CAMPAIGN.md + VERDICT.md, no FINDINGS.md). **On reading it, the arc is exemplary rather than deficient:** its VERDICT.md already carries the correction prominently and in its own voice -- "CRACKED by the B525 'Are You Sure' audit (necessary-not-sufficient) -- this headline is CORRECTED below" -- with the B1 row struck through (~~REFUTED 3-0~~), re-marked LIVE (B525-reopened), and the conflation spelled out (Bellissard gap-LABELING, a necessary K-theoretic constraint on WHERE gaps sit, read as a SUFFICIENT guarantee about WHICH gaps physically open). Nothing was missing except a file called FINDINGS.md. **The real defect: a safety invariant stated as a FILENAME.** Writer safety ("never write a verdict for an arc with no FINDINGS.md") is a good rule that held under a live 3.0% fault rate with zero fabrications, but the rule it MEANT to encode is "no verdict without a substantive findings document" -- and as a filename it silently excluded the one arc that documents its own retraction best. A safety rule that names a FILE instead of a PROPERTY will eventually refuse the wrong thing. **B519 now carries RETRACTED**, sourced from its own correction banner and B525, NOT invented -- and correct under B818's rule, since B519 withdraws its OWN headline. The invariant now reads FINDINGS.md OR VERDICT.md in both the wave-2 lock and B818's self-retraction-marker check. **The widening is guarded and deliberately narrow:** a lock asserts README.md and PREREGISTRATION.md are NOT admitted, because a prereg records INTENT not result and admitting it would let a verdict precede the work it reports. **Two locks had to move together, and that is the lesson:** writing B519's verdict immediately broke B818's marker check, because BOTH had encoded the same invariant as the same filename -- a single narrow read reproduced in two places looks like corroboration until one of them is exercised. **Still carried, not closed:** B225 carries PROVED though B745 confirmed its 2-half kill vacuous (may be correct for B225's surviving content -- needs reading, not assuming), and B58 spans three directories; B519 was closable only because its own document had already made the judgement. Gate 5 untouched.

## 2026-07-30 — B827: ten days of progress log went to a shadow file; the gate had become unable to fail
Found by the owner asking "are we always updating progresslog". **The answer was no.** 37 entries (B725 -> B826, 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-30, ten days) were written to docs/PROGRESS_LOG.md instead of this file; NONE appear here or in the sanctioned roll-off docs/progress/PROGRESS_2026-Q2.md. This session alone: 10 commits to the shadow, 3 to the real file. The shadow was created by ACCIDENT at 73d07f0e (B725); its telltale was having NO HEADER at all, opening mid-content, while this file opens "Append-only, chronological... older entries roll into docs/progress/ by quarter." **Why the gate could not catch it:** log-changelog-paired compared CHANGELOG's last-touched time against THIS file's (if tb < ta: fail). Once this file stopped being written, ta FROZE in the past, so every later CHANGELOG commit trivially satisfied tb >= ta. **A gate that watches a file nobody writes cannot detect that nobody writes it** -- it did not merely miss the defect, it had become INCAPABLE OF FAILING and would have reported PASS forever. Fail-open by DRIFT: sound when written, disarmed by a change elsewhere, no signal. The 2026-07-29 restart-resistance audit checked for gates failing open when inputs go MISSING; not for gates whose input goes STALE. **Fix:** all 37 entries migrated verbatim in original order under a heading stating what happened (their dates overlap the entries above -- a consequence of recovery, recorded rather than smoothed by re-sorting, since this file is append-only); shadow deleted; its one citation repointed (caught by path-refs, not by me). **The gate now has two checks, both able to fail:** (1) NO shadow progress log may exist outside the sanctioned archive -- the check that would have caught this on day one, with legacy/ excluded by name (a frozen pre-2026-05-28 import) so the check stays sharp rather than loosened into uselessness; (2) CHANGELOG may not run more than ONE commit ahead of PROGRESS_LOG, encoding the standing "same or next PR" rule directly -- on first run it reported "CHANGELOG is 10 commits ahead", the exact damage, measured. Negative controls run both ways. **This is the FOURTH duplicated authoritative filename found in two days** (REVIEWS.md, ROADMAP.md, PROGRESS_LOG.md, plus OI-239): nothing prevented a second file with an authoritative name from existing, and each shadow held plausible content so opening the wrong one gave no signal -- two were found by a GATE, this one by the OWNER asking a question. R35-8's repo-wide sweep is upgraded to the highest-value open instrument task; this is its first ENFORCED instance and the sweep is NOT done. **Transferable: a gate proves a property held at the moment it was written, and nothing keeps its input the same file the work is going into. Ask not "does this gate pass?" but "could it still fail?"** Gate 5 untouched.

## 2026-08-08 — B965: THE LAW_MAP SCOPE AUDIT — 165 rows, 5 flagged, ALL FIVE written today, 3 real fixes
Commissioned by the owner after B964, to catch the error class no gate can see. **METHOD, mechanical not editorial**: for each of LAW_MAP's **165** claim rows, load every arc it cites and check whether scope-limiting language present in **the arc's own verdict** is **absent from the row** (markers: only-for, scope, assumes, not-established, conditional, up-to, one-prime, not-certified, NOT-claimed, post-hoc, inferred, cited-not-re-derived, screened, necessary-not-sufficient, limits, does-not). One question, asked uniformly: **does the row claim more than its own arc does?** **THE RESULT IS THE FINDING**: 165 rows audited, **5 flagged**, **zero written before today**, **all five written today**, **3 needing real fixes**. **Zero of the older rows overclaim.** That is a diagnosis about **RATE, not competence**: the corpus built slowly is scoped correctly; the corpus built in one day is not. **ADJUDICATION.** *NO CENTRALIZER CONSTRUCTION REACHES RANK 4* **PASSES** -- it carries "SCOPE NOW UNCONDITIONAL (B960)" and names "(Steinberg)" as its citation, so the heuristic fired on an already-amended row. **FIX 1, THE TWO SEEDS**: stated an **inference as a fact** -- the shed directions U(1)_psi and U(1)_chi are **inferred from the rank bookkeeping, not computed**, which B953's own verdict says explicitly and the row did not. **FIX 2, TAU DOES DOUBLE DUTY**: presented **cited standard facts as established here** -- the three equivalences (w0 = -tau; -1 in W <=> self-dual; outer involutions = tau) are standard and were cited, not re-derived, while only tau's existence and the 63 gradings were computed. **FIX 3, THE F4 WALL IS THE GENERIC VEV**: used **"VEV" bare -- the exact error class B964 retracted ONE HOUR EARLIER** -- since every VEV in that row is a **27** VEV while adjoint VEVs are the measurement cascade and behave **oppositely**; corrected with B964's rule cited inline so the row now teaches the distinction it depends on. **WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE FAILURE MODE.** The most uncomfortable finding is FIX 3: **an error class was diagnosed, retracted, given a rule -- and then survived, unfixed, in a row written the same day. Retracting a claim does not retract its instances; a retraction needs a SWEEP, not just a correction** (registered **L139**). Second: the audit's discriminating power came entirely from comparing a row to **its own arc's verdict**, and in all three fixes **the arc's verdict was correct and properly scoped** -- the loss happened in the **summarisation step**. That localises the problem precisely: **the arcs are honest; the LAW_MAP rows compress them, and compression drops qualifiers** (registered **L140**, with a candidate gate: a row citing an arc whose verdict carries a scope marker must carry one of its own -- mechanical, and it would have caught all three). **LIMITS**: the scan is a **keyword heuristic**, can miss a scope loss phrased without its markers, and fired once on a correctly-scoped row -- a **triage tool, not a proof of correctness**; **only LAW_MAP was audited**, while CAMPAIGN_STATUS, README and the PROGRESS_LOG headlines carry compressed claims too and are **not** covered; and "zero older rows flagged" means zero flagged **by this heuristic**, not that the older corpus is clean. 7 locks, including one per fix. Gate 5 untouched.

## 2026-08-08 — B967 / L139 EXECUTED: the retraction sweep — and its first run found the retraction had never reached its own source
**THE RULE**: retracting a claim does not retract its **instances**, so a retraction is **not complete** until its phrase is registered in `docs/RETRACTED_PHRASES.md` **and the sweep is clean**. Machinery: the registry, `scripts/checks/retraction_sweep.py` sweeping **all 2,210 tracked .md files**, the gate `retraction-sweep`, and a PRACTICES row -- registered both directions. **Use vs mention** is the whole difficulty and is handled explicitly: a retracted phrase may appear inside a retraction record, a correction banner, a quotation of a former claim, or a test enforcing its absence; and incoming panel reports (PRIOR_ART_*.md, O3_PRIOR_ART.md, DRAFT_FINDINGS.md) are **evidence, not our claims**, exempt on the same principle as another seat's scripts. **WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, and it justifies the whole exercise: 11 violations across 2,210 files -- and the important one was not a stray phrase.** **B962's OWN FINDINGS still asserted BOTH claims B964 had retracted -- in its TITLE and in two body sections -- with no correction banner at all.** B964 was banked as a separate arc and **its source was never marked**; a reader arriving at B962 would have found *"nobody's object supplies a VEV, the route stops one step short"* stated as findings, with nothing to warn them. **That is precisely the failure L139 was registered to catch, and it sat in the corpus for four hours before the sweeper existed to see it.** Fixed properly rather than cosmetically: the **title retitled** (it asserted both retracted claims); a **banner added** naming both retractions and listing what still stands; and **both body sections marked inline** -- heading warnings plus struck-through corrections at the exact sentences -- because a banner at the top does not stop someone quoting section 2. The remaining hits were the correction machinery itself (mentions) and incoming panel reports; the cue list and exemptions were widened to match, **each widening justified by an inspected case** rather than to make the number go down. **NON-VACUITY DEMONSTRATED**: planting *"The object does not supply a VEV."* into docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md makes the sweep **fire**; removing it makes it **clean**; the file was restored byte-identical. **REGISTERED (5)**: the two B964 retractions, B943's priority sentence, B941's "golden power", B963's "no intermediate regime". **DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED**, with reasons recorded in the registry: *"chirality = the extremal-KMS / Galois label"* (B942), since registering it would fire on B723's own correction banner, which IS the correct treatment; and *"the Standard Model algebra"* (B950), ordinary English used correctly in many places that a grep cannot distinguish, where B892's banner and the amended LAW_MAP row are the correct treatment. **That asymmetry is the registry's main limitation and is stated rather than hidden: it can only police wording specific enough to be unambiguous -- broad phrases need banners, not greps.** **LIMITS**: phrase-exact and case-insensitive only, so a **paraphrase** of a retracted claim passes silently -- it raises the floor, it does not certify the corpus; the mention-cue list is **heuristic**; **registration is manual**, since the gate enforces that registered phrases stay dead but nothing enforces that a new retraction gets registered (that is the practices row, a human obligation); and **.md only**, with code comments and JSON verdict lines unswept. **BOTH HALVES OF THE GAP THE OWNER IDENTIFIED NOW HAVE MACHINERY**: `lawmap-scope` for the compression leak (B966/L140), `retraction-sweep` for the instance leak (B967/L139). **Neither removes the need to read.** 4 locks. Gate 5 untouched.
